newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Sierra Leone journalists denounce harassment.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone journalists denounce harassment.

text.p: Sierra Leone's journalists' association said on Tuesday that its members had been the target of unprecedented harassment and intimidation since a May 25 coup toppled civilian president Ahmad Tejan Kabbah.

The Sierra Leone Journalists' Association (SLJA) urged the ruling military junta to free three people detained during a search for a clandestine radio station broadcasting Kabbah's speeches, or hand them over to the civilian police.

"We are very concerned that in the seven weeks since the AFRC (Armed Forces Revolutionary Council) took power our members have been exposed to a degree of harassment and threats from military authorities which far exceed anything ever seen in this country," the SLJA said in a statement.
"If the military authorities consider these three persons to be guilty of the offence it is their duty to hand the matter over to the police for the appropriate action to be taken," it added.

It named the three as SLJA member Saloman Conteh and Fatmata Kamara and Jeff Bowlay Williams, arrested at the offices of The Democrat newspaper on July 8. Four other people detained at the time were released after being held for four days.

Sierra Leone's West African neighbours have denounced the coup and urged Kabbah's reinstatement. They have agreed on dialogue and economic sanctions as a first form of pressure but have retained the military option.
Regional power broker Nigeria has reinforced soldiers it had in Sierra Leone before the coup under a defence accord.
